source.title: Pi-DUAL: Using Privileged Information to Distinguish Clean from Noisy Labels
source.authors: Ke Wang; Guillermo Ortiz-Jiménez; Rodolphe Jenatton; Mark Collier; Efi Kokiopoulou; Pascal Frossard

record.tranche_reason: The paper analyzes training dynamics on realistically noisy labels using training accuracy on clean and wrong samples, rather than randomizing labels or inputs as the claim versions specify.
record.gate_note: The paper reports results for its purpose-built Pi-DUAL architecture, whose separate prediction and noise paths are designed to route clean and wrong labels. Those induced paths do not test whether standard networks naturally show the behavior. The cross-entropy baseline dynamics do bear on V6. Cited results from other studies are not recorded.
record.test_reason: The standard cross-entropy baselines measure learning dynamics on correctly and incorrectly labeled examples, bearing on V6 in a new setting with realistic human- and model-generated noise. Pi-DUAL's deliberately separated learning paths do not independently test naturally arising memorization dynamics.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors conclude that Pi-DUAL uses privileged information to separate clean-label learning from noise fitting, improving clean-test accuracy and noise detection, especially with high-quality privileged information. Their baseline analysis reports later wrong-label fitting with test degradation on CIFAR-10H and CIFAR-100N, but ignored wrong labels on ImageNet-PI (high noise).
record.recipe_differences: The paper studies a PI-based dual-path architecture and noisy-label training dynamics, not the original fully randomized-label experiment.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported cross-entropy dynamics differ by dataset: wrong-label accuracy grows alongside test-accuracy degradation on CIFAR-10H and CIFAR-100N, while the baseline ignores wrong-label samples on ImageNet-PI (high noise).
record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Machine Learning (ICML), PMLR 235, 2024
record.problems: For the relevant cross-entropy dynamics, the paper gives qualitative descriptions rather than exact curve values in text. Its datasets use realistic label noise, not fully randomized labels.
record.rows_left_out: Pi-DUAL training dynamics and the ablations in Sections 5.1 and 5.3 concern a purpose-built architecture or changes to that architecture; they do not show the behavior arising naturally in standard networks. Numerical test-accuracy and noise-detection results do not measure V6.

untested.parts: Complete random relabeling, near-zero training error, chance test performance, and unchanged architecture and hyperparameters.
Training-time comparison between true and random labels and convergence across corruption fractions.
Fitting shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or Gaussian-noise inputs.
A controlled sweep from no random label corruption to complete corruption, with perfect training fit and steadily degrading test performance.
Whether explicit regularization prevents fitting random labels and whether removing it harms generalization on true labels.
Fully random labels and a direct comparison of separate true-label and random-label training runs; the relevant baselines use mixed realistic label noise.

missing.what: Cross-entropy training accuracy on correct and wrong labels over time for CIFAR-10N (worst). Appendix C.1 reports the same findings as Section 5.1, but no row captures this additional human-noise setting.

Cross-entropy training dynamics for ImageNet-PI (low noise). Figure 6 includes this additional noise condition; its curves are not readable in the supplied text, and the blanket statement of the same findings does not establish the precise baseline trajectory.

record.verdict_notes: This is not an original source for any version. Realistic noisy labels fall within V6's stated scope. Numerical test accuracy, noise-detection AUC, and Pi-DUAL's computational overhead do not independently measure the claim versions. No exact curve values or onset times are inferred from the garbled figure extraction.

versions.untested_parts: No experiment randomizes all training labels or measures chance test error under that condition.
No comparison of training time for true versus random labels or sweep over corruption fractions.
No shuffled-pixel, permuted-pixel, or Gaussian-noise inputs.
No sweep from zero to complete random label corruption measuring training fit and test error.
No test of whether regularization or augmentation prevents fitting random labels, or whether removing it harms true-label generalization.
Uses realistic noisy labels rather than random labels; does not test the cited claim across training methods, and the cross-entropy dynamics are described qualitatively.
